segmenti.tekst: نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ الْقَصَصِ بِمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ هَٰذَا الْقُرْآنَ وَإِنْ كُنْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ
segmenti.prevod: “We relate to you the best of stories in revealing to you this Qur’an, though before it you were among the unaware.” (Yusuf 12:3)

segmenti.tekst: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ
segmenti.prevod: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and all his companions.

segmenti.tekst: After Yusuf told his father Yaqub the dream, the dream he had seen, and after his father Yaqub interpreted that dream for him – that the eleven stars he saw, the sun and the moon, were his brothers, his mother and his father – his father Yaqub says to him:
"Qala ya bunayya la taqsus ru'yaka 'ala ikhwatika fa yakidu laka kayda" – "My dear little son, do not," he says, "tell this dream to your brothers.
Do not tell this dream to your brothers, lest they plot something against you out of jealousy, or devise some plan against you, lest they destroy you."

Why does Yaqub, alayhis-salatu was-salam (peace be upon him), say this to Yusuf? Why? Because parents know their child best. Yaqub, alayhis-salam, knew his children, just as he knew Yusuf, alayhis-salam,
and he knew what they were capable of. Imagine, dear brothers: Yusuf's brothers had not heard of this dream, and despite that they planned to kill him.

And imagine if they had also heard this dream – what would they have done to him then? What would they have done to him then? The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), says: "Idha ra'a ahadukum ma yuhibbu fala yuhaddith biha illa man yuhibb." At the beginning of the hadith he says: "Ar-ru'yas-salihatu minallah" – he says: truly, a good dream is from Allah. So when one of you sees in a dream something that he likes,

he says: let him not tell it except to someone he loves. So here the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, warns us and tells us that when we see something in a dream, something good, we should not tell it except to someone we love and whom we trust, and are sure that he loves us, that he wishes us good (khayr).

Because if we tell the good thing we saw in a dream to someone who does not love us, the same thing will happen to us that happened to Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, further says: and if one of you sees in a dream something he dislikes, something that is not good, what should he do?

He says: let him blow lightly three times to his left side, let him seek refuge with Allah, and let him not tell that dream to anyone. It will not, it will not harm him. In particular, the scholars say, this is a warning to women here. Since women pay a lot of attention to these dreams, you will see – let her see something in a dream, and what does she do? As soon as she wakes up, she goes to her best friend.

And then they start picking it apart: what it is, how it is, and so on, and so on. That is why a person should keep away from these things, and when he sees a good dream, he should tell it to someone he loves.
Yaqub, alayhis-salam, further says to his son Yusuf: "Truly Shaytan, O Yusuf, truly Shaytan is an open enemy to man."

See, dear brothers, how beautifully this is said here, that is, how beautifully Yaqub put it. He did not say: "Truly, Yusuf, truly your brothers are open enemies to you"; rather, he says: "Truly Shaytan is an open enemy to man."
So it is Shaytan who sows intrigues among people. Shaytan is man's open enemy. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says in the Qur'an, conveying to us the words of Iblis.

Iblis, la'natullahi alayh (Allah's curse be upon him), says: "Wa la udillannahum ajma'in" – he says: "We will mislead them," he says, "we will mislead the sons of Adam, we will mislead them, drive them into error – wa la udillannahum wa la umanniyannahum" – and he says: "We will drive them into error and we will give them false promises." "Wa ma ya'iduhumush-shaytanu illa ghurura" – and, it says, Shaytan promises man nothing but deception. He deceives with the dunya (this world), with this [unclear], with fear, the fear of losing children and wealth and so on, and so on, and so on.

That is why a person, as the Prophet Muhammad says – we said it a little earlier – when he sees some dream, some bad dream, should turn, that is, blow lightly three times to his left side, seek refuge with Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, and not tell that dream to anyone; and the fourth thing, he says: let him change his side – so whoever was sleeping on his left side should turn onto his right, and so on.

Yaqub, alayhis-salam, further says to his son – and Yaqub, alayhis-salam, also knew how to interpret dreams – he says: since Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has given you glad tidings with this dream… And this dream that Yusuf, alayhis-salam, saw is the introduction to what will happen to him, that is, that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will send him as a prophet and give him power on Earth.
"Wa kadhalika yajtabika Rabbuka" – just as Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has given you glad tidings with this dream, Allah will also raise you up with prophethood.

"Wa yu'allimuka min ta'wilil-ahadith" – so Yaqub, his father, says: "And He will teach you the interpretation," he says, "of dreams." And you will see later what an expert Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam, is in interpreting dreams.

"Wa yutimmu ni'matahu 'alayka wa 'ala ali Ya'quba kama atammaha 'ala abawayka min qablu Ibrahima wa Ishaq. Inna Rabbaka 'alimun hakim." And He will complete His favour upon you, by sending you as a prophet, and He will complete His favour upon the family of Yaqub, because Yaqub's father was a prophet, his grandfather a prophet, he himself a prophet, and his son a prophet.
And so He will complete His favour upon the family of Yaqub, just as He completed it, that is, just as He gave that favour before him to his father and to his grandfather Ibrahim, alayhis-salam.

"Inna Rabbaka 'alimun hakim" – truly your Lord is the One who knows everything and the One who is Wise. So we see, dear brothers, that Yaqub, alayhis-salatu was-salam, was also among those who knew how to interpret, how to interpret dreams, but he did not do it, [unclear].

What does he say to his sons later? "وَأَعْلَمُ مِنَ اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ" – and he says: "I know from Allah", that is, Allah has taught me, "what you do not know", that is, what you do not know, my sons.

"I know from Allah what you do not know." So this is Yaqub's interpretation and his advice to his son. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to reward you with every good for listening attentively. I ask Him, the Exalted, to forgive us our sins. I ask Him, the Exalted, that we, in sha Allah, complete this tafsir by the end of the month of Ramadan. Amin.
